cleanIntro: The single-tube 12-gauge bullpup, 6+1, with a carry handle instead of a rail. Its field strip shares three steps with the KSG family and then diverges completely: the KS7's barrel is held by ONE mag cap under magazine-spring pressure, not by two magazine bolts. Kel-Tec ends the strip with barrel and receiver apart, so there is no Deep Clean path.

steps.title: Confirm you have the KS7, not one of the dual-tube guns
steps.action: Confirm the shotgun has ONE magazine tube, a fibre-glass reinforced carry handle over the barrel with a fibre optic front sight, M-LOK slots rather than a picatinny rail, and a mag cap at the muzzle end. No selector.
steps.prose: The KS7 is the odd one in this six-gun book: every other shotgun it covers has two magazine tubes and a selector between them, and most of the manual's procedures are tagged for those. The physical tells are quick — one tube, a mag cap where the KSG has two slotted bolts, a carry handle instead of a rail, 6+1 rather than 6+6+1, and about 5.9 pounds against the KSG's 6.9. Get this wrong at the barrel and you will be looking for magazine bolts that do not exist.
steps.quote: KelTec also has a single magazine fed, pump action shotgun variant, the KS7.
steps.cite: KSG KSG COMPACT KSG TACTICAL KSG25 KSG410 KS7 SHOTGUNS SAFETY, INSTRUCTION & PARTS MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision or edition code printed on any page — B. Overview — Description (ALL SHOTGUNS), p.5

steps.title: Read the variant tag on every heading before you follow it
steps.action: Before following any step in this manual, check whether its heading is tagged (ALL SHOTGUNS), (ALL KSG VARIANTS, KSG410) or (KS7). Only the first and the last are yours.
steps.prose: Kel-Tec wrote one book for six shotguns and marked the difference in headings rather than splitting the manual. That makes the tag the most important text on the page. Loading, the barrel separation and the barrel joining all exist in two versions, and the KSG version of each is printed close enough to the KS7 version that a glance can land on the wrong one. Adjacency on the page is not applicability.
steps.quote: NOTE: your particular variant may or may not have information in each section; this manual should be read and understood in its entirety.
steps.cite: KSG KSG COMPACT KSG TACTICAL KSG25 KSG410 KS7 SHOTGUNS SAFETY, INSTRUCTION & PARTS MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision or edition code printed on any page — B. Overview — Description (ALL SHOTGUNS), p.5
steps.warn: Anything tagged (ALL KSG VARIANTS, KSG410) is a two-magazine-tube procedure and does not apply to the KS7.

steps.title: Safety on, action forward, empty the tube at the cartridge catch
steps.action: Point the muzzle safely, ensure the action is locked forward, and press the safety until the white S shows. Rotate the outer cartridge catch down, away from the shells, to release them from the magazine tube.
steps.prose: There is only one tube on a KS7, so this happens once — but the shells still leave with force and want catching. The tube is empty when the magazine follower is visible through the ejection port, which is the confirmation the manual asks for rather than a count. Note the KS7 is a light shotgun and the manual warns its recoil with full-power loads is sharp; that is worth knowing before you decide what to reload it with afterwards.
steps.quote: Rotate outer cartridge catch down (away from the shells) to release one or more shells from the magazine tube. NOTE: shells will eject with some force from the magazine tube.
steps.cite: KSG KSG COMPACT KSG TACTICAL KSG25 KSG410 KS7 SHOTGUNS SAFETY, INSTRUCTION & PARTS MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision or edition code printed on any page — C. Operation Instructions — Unloading (ALL SHOTGUNS), step 4, p.14

steps.title: Action fully rearward, then check the chamber by eye and by finger
steps.action: Slide the action fully rearward and check the chamber both visually and by touch to confirm the shotgun is unloaded.
steps.prose: The KS7's loading and ejection share one port under the receiver behind the grip, so you are checking upward into a shadowed opening — which is exactly why the manual asks for a finger as well as a look. Do it with the action fully back so the lifters are down and out of the way. Keep the support hand on the action between the marked arrows; behind the handguard it short-strokes and pinches.
steps.quote: With the action fully rearward, always visually and tactually check the chamber to confirm the firearm is unloaded.
steps.cite: KSG KSG COMPACT KSG TACTICAL KSG25 KSG410 KS7 SHOTGUNS SAFETY, INSTRUCTION & PARTS MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision or edition code printed on any page — C. Operation Instructions — Unloading (ALL SHOTGUNS), step 8, p.14

steps.title: Pull the two frame pins and park them in the retaining holes
steps.action: With the safety on, pull the two frame pins beside the ejection port out of the grip assembly and push them into the retaining holes provided on the shotgun.
steps.prose: These two pins carry the entire grip and fire control, and the retaining holes exist so they are never loose on a bench. Pins in the holes as soon as they are out. They should move under thumb pressure; if they resist, the grip is loaded against them and needs to be held square. The KS7 has no magazine selector to centre first — that step in the manual is tagged 'if applicable' and applies to the dual-tube guns.
steps.quote: Remove the frame pins adjacent to the ejection port located on the grip assembly and place them in the retaining holes as shown below.
steps.cite: KSG KSG COMPACT KSG TACTICAL KSG25 KSG410 KS7 SHOTGUNS SAFETY, INSTRUCTION & PARTS MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision or edition code printed on any page — D. Field Strip — Removal of Grip Assembly (ALL SHOTGUNS), step 3, p.15
steps.warn: Always wear safety glasses when disassembling the firearm to protect your eyes from components that are under pressure, such as springs.

steps.title: Rotate the grip assembly up and off, then draw the stock rearward
steps.action: Rotate the rear of the grip assembly directly upwards to lift it clear. Then grip the stock and pull it straight rearward off the receiver.
steps.prose: The grip pivots off a catch at its front, so lifting the rear is what releases it — pulling downward achieves nothing. The stock then slides straight out of the back of the receiver with no fastener at all; it carries the lifter arms with it, which is why it must be off before the bolt will come out. Pull it square. On the KS7 a plastic notch in the stock protrudes into a slot in the receiver, and that alignment has to be met again on the way back in.
steps.quote: Remove the grip assembly by rotating the rear of the assembly directly upwards as shown below.
steps.cite: KSG KSG COMPACT KSG TACTICAL KSG25 KSG410 KS7 SHOTGUNS SAFETY, INSTRUCTION & PARTS MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision or edition code printed on any page — D. Field Strip — Removal of Grip Assembly (ALL SHOTGUNS), step 4, p.16

steps.title: Action to the rear, then lift the bolt out
steps.action: Move the forend to its rearmost position to reach the bolt, then reach in, rotate the bolt onto its side and lift it out of the receiver.
steps.prose: Forward, the bolt is locked into the barrel extension and there is nothing to take hold of; all the way back, it sits loose in the receiver. It comes out rotated onto its side because upright it will not pass the opening. Look at the bolt lock's angled bottom section as it leaves — that face has to meet the bolt carrier's angled section again on assembly, and a bolt set on the carrier the wrong way is the usual reason a reassembled bullpup will not lock up.
steps.quote: The bolt should now be resting in the receiver of the shotgun and can be easily removed by reaching in and rotating the bolt on its side.
steps.cite: KSG KSG COMPACT KSG TACTICAL KSG25 KSG410 KS7 SHOTGUNS SAFETY, INSTRUCTION & PARTS MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision or edition code printed on any page — D. Field Strip — Removal of the Bolt (ALL SHOTGUNS), step 2, p.16

steps.title: The KS7's barrel is held by ONE mag cap — and it is spring loaded
steps.action: Rotate the mag cap on the front of the shotgun counter-clockwise to remove it. Keep a hand on it the whole way: the magazine spring is behind it.
steps.prose: This is where the KS7 parts company with every other shotgun in this book. There are no magazine bolts to alternate — one mag cap holds the barrel assembly on, and it is under heavy pressure from the magazine spring the moment the threads let go. Hold it, unscrew it slowly and let the spring extend under control. The threads are fine pitch, so ease it off square rather than cocking it. Once the cap is off, the magazine spring and follower can be lifted out and put somewhere safe.
steps.quote: The barrel assembly is secured to the receiver assembly by the mag cap, located on the front of the firearm.
steps.cite: KSG KSG COMPACT KSG TACTICAL KSG25 KSG410 KS7 SHOTGUNS SAFETY, INSTRUCTION & PARTS MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision or edition code printed on any page — D. Field Strip — Separation of the Barrel and Receiver Assemblies (KS7), step 1, p.17
steps.warn: The mag cap is under heavy spring pressure from the magazine spring and may cause injury if unintentionally released from the firearm.

steps.title: Slide the barrel assembly off the receiver
steps.action: With the mag cap, magazine spring and follower removed and set aside, pull the barrel assembly and the receiver assembly linearly apart.
steps.prose: The separation is a straight pull along the bore axis — nothing hinges, nothing rotates. The action and bolt carrier may stay attached to the receiver, which the manual shows as the normal field-stripped state, so do not try to persuade them off. What you should be holding is a barrel assembly, a receiver assembly with the carrier and forend, the bolt, the stock, the grip, the frame pins, and the mag cap with its spring and follower.
steps.quote: The barrel assembly may slide off the receiver assembly by pulling linearly apart, as shown below.
steps.cite: KSG KSG COMPACT KSG TACTICAL KSG25 KSG410 KS7 SHOTGUNS SAFETY, INSTRUCTION & PARTS MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision or edition code printed on any page — D. Field Strip — Separation of the Barrel and Receiver Assemblies (KS7), step 4, p.18

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Barrel assembly, receiver assembly with bolt carrier and forend, bolt, stock assembly, grip assembly, frame pins, mag cap, magazine spring and follower. That is Kel-Tec's whole published strip for the KS7.
steps.prose: Everything the cleaning section names is now reachable: the bolt and receiver exteriors, the bore and chamber, the breech of the barrel and the barrel extension, and the magazine tube — which on a KS7 you can clean right through, since the spring and follower are out. That is a real advantage this variant has over the dual-tube guns. Going past this point is tied to the warranty, which is void if the firearm is disassembled beyond the instructions in the manual.
steps.quote: Further disassembly should only be performed by a certified gunsmith or KelTec. Attempting further disassembly could void your warranty.
steps.cite: KSG KSG COMPACT KSG TACTICAL KSG25 KSG410 KS7 SHOTGUNS SAFETY, INSTRUCTION & PARTS MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision or edition code printed on any page — D. Field Strip, closing note, p.20

deepAbsentReason: The combined shotgun manual publishes one level of disassembly, headed "D. FIELD STRIP", and closes it with a note that further disassembly should only be performed by a certified gunsmith or KelTec and could void the warranty; the Limitations of Warranty section repeats it as a voiding condition. Its cleaning section carries a single tier keyed to "after every shooting session" with no deeper interval and no further procedure. The only variant-specific procedures printed past the KS7 field strip belong to the dual-magazine-tube guns and are their assembly steps, not a deeper KS7 strip. Nothing deeper is published for the KS7, so there is no Deep Clean to walk.

cleaning.name: BOLT, RECEIVER & BREECH
tasks: Thoroughly clean all exterior sides of the bolt and receiver with solvent and a brush
Small brush dipped in solvent around the breech of the barrel and the barrel extension and all adjacent areas that have taken powder or primer residue
Clean the feedramps on the bottom of the bolt carrier — on the KS7 those are what shells ride over on their way into the tube

cleaning.name: BORE & MAGAZINE TUBE
tasks: Brush the barrel bore and chamber with a good powder-removing solvent and bore brush, then wipe clean with patches or a swab
With the spring and follower out, run a brush the full length of the single magazine tube — plastic wad residue coats it and is what makes a follower stick
Wipe the magazine spring and follower and check the follower slides freely before it goes back

cleaning.name: OIL & FUNCTION
tasks: Use a cloth to apply a light coating of high-quality gun oil to all internal and external metal surfaces, let it soak into the external surfaces about five minutes, then wipe clean
Never use automotive brake cleaner or any solvent not designed for polymer firearms
Manually cycle the action back and forth to check the function of the firearm before it is put away

reassembly: Place the barrel assembly on top of the receiver assembly and slide it into the receiver; ensure the magazine tube protrudes through the muzzle plate and the barrel extension bottoms out against the receiver so the two surfaces touch.
Add the follower, then the magazine spring into the hollow cavity in the follower, then the mag cap onto the spring.
Compress the magazine spring so the mag cap can be threaded on; the threads are fine pitch, so start it carefully by hand and rotate clockwise until the cap stops on the muzzle plate.
Move the action to its rearmost position and set the bolt onto the bolt carrier — the bolt lock's bottom angled section attaches to the carrier's angled section.
Slide the action fully forward, which should lock the bolt into the barrel extension.
Slide the stock into the receiver with the lifter arms passing either side of the bolt, and make sure the plastic notch in the stock protrudes into the slot in the receiver — that check is KS7 only.
Place the front of the grip into the grip catch, rotate the grip down onto the receiver, align the frame pin holes and fit the frame pins.
Cycle the action to confirm it functions, and re-check every accessory on the carry handle is still tight.
fncheck: With the magazine tube emptied and the chamber checked: press down the action release and cycle the action through its full travel — it should run smoothly and lock forward. Check the barrel extension and receiver surfaces are touching with no gap and that the mag cap is fully seated on the muzzle plate. The safety should only engage with the hammer cocked, showing white S for safe and red F for fire. Confirm the follower moves down the tube and is visible at the ejection port when the tube is empty, and that the carry handle and any M-LOK accessory on it are tight — the handle carries the front sight, so a loose one moves your point of aim.
